title: Horse Powertrain reveals a 4.0-litre hybrid V8 for Lotus's first supercar
extract: The production-ready HORSE W40 is a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 rated at more than 500kW and 800Nm, paired with an eight-speed hybrid dual-clutch transmission. The powertrain is set to debut in Lotus's Type 135, the marque's first supercar.

title: Nissan cuts petrol-car production in China as EV and plug-in hybrid demand accelerates
extract: Nissan says the shift to new-energy vehicles in China is happening faster than expected, so it will scale back local petrol-car output and expand battery-electric and plug-in hybrid production. The change follows steeply lower sales in the country and highlights the divergent pace of electrification across markets.

title: Google DeepMind uses AI to formally verify key parts of Signal's encryption protocol
extract: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code framework helped researchers mathematically verify several of Signal's core cryptographic guarantees in a four-week proof of concept. The work did not verify the entire app, but the team is releasing its specification and proofs to support further formal-verification research.

title: Yandex says 2.84% of cloud customer data is permanently lost after attacks
extract: Yandex says it has restored 97.16% of customer data after attacks damaged three data centres, but the remaining 2.84% cannot be recovered because of equipment damage and missing customer backups. The company says it plans to enable backups by default and spread cloud resources across more independent locations.

title: Helsing launches Clarity battlefield intelligence software built around AI agents
extract: Helsing's Clarity software combines information from drones, satellites, military reports and open-source intelligence to help identify assets and assess possible responses. The company says its specialist agents expose supporting evidence, while human operators remain responsible for approving any strike.

title: AI agents used by Kazakhstan-linked hackers to steal 2,000 Tajik government documents
extract: Researchers say the espionage group used Hermes, an open-source autonomous-agent framework, to plan reconnaissance, run hacking commands and organise stolen files. The exposed operation shows how attackers are beginning to delegate substantial parts of cyber intrusions to AI agents.

title: UK AI-chip startup Fractile raises $720m at a $7bn valuation
extract: London- and Bristol-based Fractile has raised $720 million in a Series C round, valuing the company at $7 billion. It is developing chips for AI inference that it says can deliver faster responses while reducing energy use and cost, with backing that includes the UK's Sovereign AI fund.

title: United Airlines moves to block AI agents from its digital platforms over security concerns
extract: United plans to restrict AI bots across its websites and booking channels, warning that sharing account credentials can expose personal data or trigger unintended purchases and account changes. It also cites regulatory risks when automated agents perform actions such as flight check-in.

title: Samsung's new HBM chip-packaging plant to trigger $30bn in additional investment
extract: South Korea says Samsung's new high-bandwidth-memory packaging facility in Asan will be followed by roughly 40 trillion won in advanced-equipment investment. The three-floor clean-room production line is scheduled to begin operating in June 2028 to meet demand for server memory.

title: PlayStation 3 turns 20: a retrospective on Sony's Cell-powered console
extract: The Japanese launch anniversary revisits the PS3's unusual Cell Broadband Engine, co-developed with IBM and Toshiba, and the development challenges it created. The console eventually sold 87.4 million units and helped bring Blu-ray, HDMI and standard 1080p output to the mainstream console market.

title: 1985 arcade racer Shot Rider joins Arcade Archives on modern consoles
extract: Seibu Kaihatsu's motorcycle-themed vertical racer is being added to Hamster's Arcade Archives, with release scheduled for 12 November 2026. The modern release adds score-focused modes, while the Arcade Archives 2 editions also include a time-attack mode.

title: Rare Mega Drive RPG Twinkle Tale gets its first official release outside Japan
extract: The 1992 Japan-only action RPG is receiving newly localised Mega Drive / Genesis cartridges from Retro-Bit and Limited Run Games. Pre-orders opened on 10 November, with the individually numbered collector's edition expected to ship in March 2027.

title: Morning Star is a new Golden Axe-inspired homebrew beat-'em-up for Mega Drive
extract: A five-person team has announced a work-in-progress Mega Drive game inspired by Golden Axe and Dungeons & Dragons. The developers are targeting four playable heroes, two-player co-op, magic attacks and mountable creatures.

title: iMSX2 emulator update brings MSX games to Apple Watch
extract: The iMSX2.8 update lets users sync MSX ROMs, disk images and saves from an iPhone to an Apple Watch, then run games on the watch's tiny display with touch controls. The emulator is built around C-BIOS to reproduce the original MSX environment.

title: NES platformer 8 Eyes is being lined up for enhanced SNES, Mega Drive and GBA versions
extract: Piko Interactive is seeking crowdfunding for enhanced versions of the 1988 NES action-adventure, with upgraded graphics and sound planned for SNES, Mega Drive and GBA. A special NES commemorative edition is also planned, although the campaign launch date has not yet been announced.

title: The Guardian's latest science-fiction, fantasy and horror roundup covers five new novels
extract: Lisa Tuttle's roundup spans an AI-governed near-future Icelandic mystery, a dark fantasy about magical story worlds, illustrated horror, Chinese speculative fiction and a surreal comic fantasy. The selection includes Alfa, The Lost Spectacular, Look What the Cat Dragged In, China +100 and Everything Happens So Much.

title: But Can It Run Doom? book Kickstarter explores the game's many unlikely ports
extract: Boss Fight Books has launched a Kickstarter for David L. Craddock's 224-page history of Doom's PC origins, console conversions and unusual hardware adaptations. A special edition adds interviews with John Carmack, Tom Hall, John Romero and soundtrack composer Aubrey Hodges.

title: PlayStation: The First 30 Years is a lavish visual history built from Sony's archives
extract: Read-Only Memory's large-format book draws on Sony's hardware archives and exclusive interviews with Ken Kutaragi, Teiyu Goto and Yujin Morisawa. It documents prototypes, design sketches, debug hardware and the engineering history behind the PlayStation family.

title: Forgotten Worlds issue 9 revisits the TurboGrafx-16 and PC Engine
extract: The 100-page ninth issue of Forgotten Worlds focuses on NEC's PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16, covering its hardware, games, packaging and marketing history. It also includes interviews with former NEC USA manager John Podlasek and PC Engine programmer Hiromasa Iwasaki.
